\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{منتشر} \fa{کردن} (montasher kardan)}{منتشر کردن (montasher kardan)}]{\fa{منتشر} \fa{کردن} (montasher kardan) — to publish, to release}

\label{lesson:FA-C312-montasher-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for details, then the Persian for a news agency.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{منتشر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{منتشر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{montasher kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to publish, to release\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روزنامه} \fa{عکس} \fa{های} \fa{جشن} \fa{را} \fa{منتشر} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ruznâme 'aks-hâ-ye jashn râ montasher kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The newspaper published the photos of the celebration.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{montasher mikonad}; the passive is \emph{montasher shod}. \emph{montasher} means \textquotedblleft{}spread, published\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{montasher} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{muntashir}, \textquotedblleft{}spread out\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{montasher kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{montasher kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{montasher kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for details, then the Persian for a news agency, then say \emph{montasher kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پخش} \fa{کردن} (pakhsh kardan)}{پخش کردن (pakhsh kardan)}]{\fa{پخش} \fa{کردن} (pakhsh kardan) — to broadcast; to hand out}

\label{lesson:FA-C312-pakhsh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a news agency, then the Persian for to publish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پخش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پخش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{pakhsh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to broadcast; to hand out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تلویزیون} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{را} \fa{زنده} \fa{پخش} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Televiziyon mosâbeqe râ zende pakhsh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The television broadcast the match live.
\end{quote}

Also \textquotedblleft{}to hand out, to spread\textquotedblright{}: \emph{shirini pakhsh kard} \textquotedblleft{}he handed out sweets\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{pakhsh mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pakhsh} \textquotedblleft{}spread, scattered\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word whose deeper origin is not settled; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pakhsh kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pakhsh kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a news agency, then the Persian for to publish, then say \emph{pakhsh kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گوینده} (guyande)}{گوینده (guyande)}]{\fa{گوینده} (guyande) — a newsreader, an announcer}

\label{lesson:FA-C312-guyande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to publish, then the Persian for to broadcast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گوینده}}
\textbf{\fa{گوینده}} (\emph{guyande}) — \textquotedblleft{}a newsreader, an announcer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{گوینده} \fa{اخبار} \fa{با} \fa{صدای} \fa{آرام} \fa{صحبت} \fa{میکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Guyande-ye akhbâr bâ sedâ-ye ârâm sohbat mikard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The newsreader spoke in a calm voice.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}one who says\textquotedblright{}: \emph{gu-}, the present stem of \emph{goftan}, + \emph{-ande}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{guyande} is the present stem \emph{gu-} of \emph{goftan} \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{} with the native suffix \emph{-ande} \textquotedblleft{}one who\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB lists the word with no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بیننده} (binande)}{بیننده (binande)}]{\fa{بیننده} (binande) — a viewer}

\label{lesson:FA-C312-binande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to broadcast, then the Persian for a newsreader.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بیننده}}
\textbf{\fa{بیننده}} (\emph{binande}) — \textquotedblleft{}a viewer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{میلیون} \fa{ها} \fa{بیننده} \fa{این} \fa{برنامه} \fa{را} \fa{تماشا} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Milyon-hâ binande in barnâme râ tamâshâ kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Millions of viewers watched this programme.
\end{quote}

\emph{bin-}, the present stem of \emph{didan} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{-ande}. Plural \emph{binandegân} or \emph{binande-hâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{binande} is \emph{bin-}, the present stem of \emph{didan} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}, with the native suffix \emph{-ande} \textquotedblleft{}one who\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پوشش} \fa{خبری} (pushesh-e khabari)}{پوشش خبری (pushesh-e khabari)}]{\fa{پوشش} \fa{خبری} (pushesh-e khabari) — news coverage}

\label{lesson:FA-C312-pushesh-e-khabari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a newsreader, then the Persian for a viewer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پوشش} \fa{خبری}}
\textbf{\fa{پوشش} \fa{خبری}} (\emph{pushesh-e khabari}) — \textquotedblleft{}news coverage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{جشن} \fa{پوشش} \fa{خبری} \fa{زیادی} \fa{داشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In jashn pushesh-e khabari-ye ziyâdi dâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This celebration got a lot of news coverage.
\end{quote}

\emph{pushesh} \textquotedblleft{}covering\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{pushidan} \textquotedblleft{}to cover, to wear\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{khabari} \textquotedblleft{}of the news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pushesh} \textquotedblleft{}covering\textquotedblright{} is native Persian, from \emph{pushidan} \textquotedblleft{}to cover, to wear\textquotedblright{}. \emph{khabari} adds the Persian \emph{-i} to \emph{khabar} \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{khabar} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
